title: The Heart of Angular: Reactive UI Updates

scenes.line1: How does Angular keep your UI fresh?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Angular updates your app instantly when data changes? Let's crack the core idea that powers it all.

scenes.label: Component
scenes.sub: A component is a TypeScript class, template, and optional CSS.
scenes.say: First up: everything in Angular starts with a component. It's just a class, a template, and maybe some styles.
Data binding connects your logic to the view. Properties push data out. Events pull actions in. Two-way binding keeps both in sync.
For reactivity, Angular uses observables for streams, but now signals for local state. Signals update the view automatically, no subscription needed.

scenes.label: ChangeDetect
scenes.sub: Default checks all; OnPush checks only on input change.
scenes.say: Change detection is the engine. By default, Angular checks everything. OnPush only checks when data changes—faster for big apps.

scenes.question: Does DI update the view?
scenes.wrong: Yes, injecting a service triggers updates.
scenes.right: No, DI just gives you the service. The view updates when data changes, not when a service is injected.
scenes.say: Watch out: injecting a service doesn’t update your UI. Only data changes or signals do.
